HIDDEN (supporting). Question: is PS94's loss on the frozen behavioral-state decoder a problem with the state definitions? Decoders: frozen pre-stroke 3-way logistic (quiet / running / licking, 1 s segments, 4 x 0.25 s bins, joint-LocaNMF basis), PRODUCTION version = per-session z-scored features + the stored scaling=session_z models (commit abda8c9c), pre column leave-one-session-out; within-session refit = same pipeline, GroupKFold by period inside each session; class-balanced z = diagnostic only (session mean = mean of the three class means), fitted in memory, never stored. Numbers, PS94 pre / acute / subacute / chronic (session means): production balanced accuracy .98 / .91 / .81 / .78; refit .98 / .99 / .98 / .98; class-balanced z .99 / .97 / .94 / .90. Production per-class recall: quiet .98 / .91 / .95 / .95, running .98 / .84 / .54 / .49, licking .99 / 1.00 / .94 / .90. Pooled confusion, chronic: running read as quiet .29, as licking .24. PS92 / PS93 / PS95 stay .89-.99 under every arm. Mechanism (likely): PS94 runs far more post-stroke (7 % of time above 3 mm/s pre, 14 % post; ~10 % of segments pre vs ~40 % post) and faster (median running speed ~7 -> ~15 mm/s), so the per-session z-score (mean over all segments) is pulled toward running and running segments shift toward the other classes; the class-balanced z-score removes most of the loss. Correction: the earlier 11-02 reading (PS94 loses its LICKING class, licking read as quiet .49) came from the pre-fix UNSCALED decoder; under the production z-scored decoder licking is intact and running is what fails. Running-class recall pooled (13pos): .98 / .92 / .83 / .89 (pre-fix .99 / .95 / .86 / .92); acute keeps ~94 % (was ~96-97 %); boot_delta vs pre (animals -> sessions) -.04 [-.12, .01] / -.12 [-.34, .02] / -.12 [-.37, .02], none significant; per animal acute .95 / .99 / .84 / 1.00 (PS95 one session). Open decision for Priya: adopt a class-balanced session z-score for the state decoder (new spec id) or keep the plain one and report PS94's running loss as a scaling sensitivity. Gate: camera gate for attempts ; cam1 table UNKNOWN

Attempt = hit + incomplete lick on a far-contra trial (cam4 + cam1 lick events, DAQ contact), engaged trials, rebuilt trial_attempts.csv (10-25); n trials acute 336 / 292 / 450 / 120 (PS95 = one session). Completion back to .95-.99 chronically. Licks without contact: cam4 no-contact licks + cam1-only no-contact events, far_R only; chronically still raised only in PS92 / PS94 (.35 / .35 / .55 / .32). paragraphs: + = contralesional. 'Launch' starts at the first tracked frame (~1.5 mm out); 250 Hz resolves submovements ≥ ~20 ms. Open markers = sessions; filled = pooled, 95 % CI

notes: Encoding page Fig 14.18 S21 (recovery analysis 1, Priya 10-30; Bollu T, Ito BS, Whitehead SC, Kardon B, Redd J, Liu MH, Goldberg JH (2021) Cortex-dependent corrections as the tongue reaches for and misses targets. Nature 594:82-87: corrective submovements are ALM-dependent). S21b [#f-lick_recovery_primary]: 250 Hz 3-D tongue, far-contralesional spout, cued post-cue licks (all orders and outcomes), PS92-95, August pre. Launch angle = direction of the first 12 ms of protrusion; endpoint = angle at the extension peak; both relative to the animal's pre-stroke hits. Corrective submovement (CSM) = an extra speed peak above a noise-calibrated threshold (50 mm/s; noise alone 5 % of licks vs 15.6 % real, pre). Pre-stroke the Bollu signatures hold: CSMs 0.28-0.33 at far side spouts vs 0.04-0.08 at close spouts. After the stroke the launch is aimed ipsilesionally (-26 deg acute, -7 subacute, 4/4) and recovers (-3 chronic, n.s.). The endpoint follows the launch; the within-lick correction does not change in any epoch, and the CSM share FALLS (-0.13 / -0.15 / -0.14, 3-4/4). Reading: the brain fixes the launch command itself rather than adding feedback corrections; in-flight correction is IMPAIRED early (toward-target correction -5.1 deg acutely; missed later licks lose their pre-stroke re-aim, 4/4; within-lick gain dips subacutely) and recovers chronically, but never exceeds pre, so it is not the route to recovery. Stats: pooled session level with 95 % nested bootstrap CI; top-band * = CI excludes 0 AND >= 3/4 animals same sign; ** = also Holm over the 9 primary tests. Caveats: 'launch' starts at the first tracked frame (~1.5 mm out), so it includes where the tongue emerges; 250 Hz resolves only submovements >= ~20 ms; launch noise 5-8 deg per lick. Licks: LP video licks (cam4) with 3-D tongue paths; pre reference ('hits') = pre licks with a DAQ spout contact. Script scripts/within_lick_correction.py; prereg + outcome docs/status/WITHIN_LICK_CORRECTION_PREREG_20261030.md. PROVISIONAL, n = 4.

paragraphs: •  A decoder refit after the stroke reads lick position again (90–100 % of pre)
•  The frozen read-out stays at ~75 % for ITI licks, read contralesional of where they land

notes: PANELS SHOWN: B and C of Key figure 1 (A, behavior, is the behavior slide's far-contra story; D is the next slide). Encoding page Key figure 1 (scripts/key_figure.py). A BEHAVIOR: far-contra FIRST-cued-lick aim offset vs the animal's pre landing (deg, - = ipsilesional): pre -1.5, acute -29.4, subacute -14.0, chronic -8.5; 25 % of the acute deficit remains chronically (per animal 16 / 24 / 45 / 10 %). B CUED licks, fraction of pre (mean of animals, 95 % paired nested CI): frozen far-contra spout code on far-contra hits 0.26 / 0.69 / 0.70; frozen lateral lick decoder 0.80 -> 0.93; decoder REFIT per epoch (vs matched-n pre) 0.90 / 0.96 / 1.00 (Fig 10.2b). C ITI licks: frozen 0.74 / 0.78 / 0.76 (4/4 every epoch); refit 0.89 / 0.94 / 0.97. D ITI like-for-like offset (all ITI licks): +0.37 [+0.16, +0.58] / +0.23 / +0.28 mm (4/4 each); against pre licks of the SAME previous-trial target too (12.15) +0.26 / +0.16 / +0.24 (4/4 each). Survives kinematic + FaceRhythm covariates (5-7 % explained, 12.16 [#f-lick_covref_offset]) and a non-linear decoder (11.20 [#f-lick_nonlinear_decoder]); a face / tongue-only decoder loses no ITI position information (11.21 [#f-lick_behaviour_decoder]): the change is in cortex, not the movement. SIGN: + = READ more contralesional than the lick landed (decoder like-for-like offset, a DIRECTION quantity; page sign-conventions box); landing / decoded lateral position + = contralesional; image left = ipsilesional. Decoder: frozen pre-stroke KEY-row lateral lick-position decoder per lick set (z-scored Allen areas with the ALM / tjM1 split, lags 0-0.2 s, August pre sessions, pre scored leave-one-session-out). Licks: LP video licks (cam4 detector) with 3-D tongue position from cam1 + cam4 pose. LIKE-FOR-LIKE offset = each lick's decoded lateral position minus a Gaussian-weighted mean (sigma 0.1 mm, chosen by held-out pre prediction) of the decoded positions of the animal's PRE licks of the same set that LANDED at the same lateral place (any spout, no bins); 0.5 % of licks without a reference. Session means; change vs pre, 95 % paired nested bootstrap (animals -> sessions), * = CI excludes 0, k/n animals. ITI = licks between trials; DOCKED-SPOUT ITI = onset while the spout is docked (~35 % of ITI licks; Priya's primary ITI set, 10-29; frozen all-ITI decoder, nothing refit). PROVISIONAL (n = 4).

paragraphs: Offset component (mm, mean of animals) by epoch; left ITI licks, right cued licks. The cross-animal cvR² panels of the figure are in the notes

notes: Encoding page Fig 12.17 [#f-lick_offset_terms] (KEY; Priya 10-29: 'prioritize the ITI per-area decomposition'). The frozen lateral decoder is linear, so each session's like-for-like offset = sum_k beta_k dh_k (dh = the feature's change vs pre licks that landed at the same place). Each left / right pair splits EXACTLY into a DIFFERENCE part 1/2(beta_r - beta_l)(dh_r - dh_l) and a SHARED part 1/2(beta_r + beta_l)(dh_r + dh_l). ITI offset acute +0.39 = difference +0.29 (75 %) + shared +0.16 + unpaired -0.06; chronic +0.29 = +0.20 (70 %) + 0.15 - 0.07; orofacial + SSs carry it all (+0.42 / +0.32), the rest of cortex nets ~0; SSp-n difference alone +0.34 acute / +0.20 chronic. Cued: acute +0.17 = +0.10 difference + 0.09 shared, ~0 afterwards. Against recovery (unseen-animal cvR2, bottom row of the page figure, not shown): only the total ITI offset transfers across animals (0.34 vs days 0.17); the components do not (per-animal scales). Within animals the SSp-n difference term tracks recovery in 4 / 4 in every set: ITI -> ITI angle r -0.66 / -0.72 / -0.51 / -0.45, ITI -> cued aim -0.66 / -0.65 / -0.60 / -0.46, cued -> aim -0.94 / -0.84 / -0.84 / -0.69 (within-animal mixed model p < 0.001 each); shared parts flip sign between animals. For CUED licks the offset is ~0 chronically (-0.02 mm), so the cued correlation reflects the acute -> chronic course; for ITI licks the term stays raised chronically (+0.19 mm). Reading: the recovery-relevant part is a hemispheric difference in SSp-n (nose / upper-lip S1) as the pre-stroke decoder weights it. Licks: LP video licks (cam4) with 3-D tongue position. Script scripts/lick_offset_terms_recovery.py. PROVISIONAL.

Fig 14.9 (KEY), cued row. Pairs ALM, tjM1, SSp-m, SSp-n: X_right (contralesional) vs X_left (ipsilesional), raw dF/F, same traces as Fig 14.7; per session and spout log2(contra AUC / ipsi AUC). Pre: tjM1 close ipsi +.36 to +.52, close contra -.37 to -.73, far contra -.36 to -.69 in every animal. Post (cued, 0-0.5 s): far contra tjM1 +.54 / +.32 / +.32 (4/4 every epoch), SSp-n +.88 / +.55 / +.55; far mid +.25 / +.12 / +.17; far ipsi +.07 / +.19 / +.20 while close ipsi stays ~0, so the rebalancing may follow reach distance as well as direction (close vs far: Fig 14.11). Pooling the four areas only modestly cuts noise (they are strongly correlated). Same measure as the read-out offset's balance term (section 4, Figs 12.17-12.21). Licks: LP video licks (cam4), engaged trials. PROVISIONAL.

paragraphs: Shown as implied direction = −(balance); top: sessions (gray = pre, left out), mixed models with log(day); bottom: cross-validated R², balance (red) vs days since stroke (gray)

notes: Encoding page Fig 14.18 [#f-lick_recovery_primary] (KEY; first image of the block, lick_recovery_primary_full.png = every first post-cue lick, 10-29); columns cued first lick -> aim and ITI first lick after quiet -> ITI angle (the ITI -> cued aim column is on the page). Balance = angle-matched GAIN RATIO, log2(contralesional activity / what the animal's pre licks at the same angle and order predict) - log2(same, ipsilesional), baseline-subtracted (-1..-0.5 s), 0.1-0.5 s after the FIRST lick, pooled over ALM, tjM1, SSp-m, SSp-n and SSs. Display = implied direction = -(balance). Cued first lick -> far-contra aim: per-animal r .71 / .82 / .94 / .75; within-animal +12.6 deg per log2 unit (p .001); cross-validated R2 for an unseen animal .70 (capped licks; .65 uncapped, shown) vs days .23; .53 without extrapolated licks; .63 with a kinematics-matched reference. ITI -> ITI angle: r .58 / .80 / .91 / .10, unseen animal .42 (days .17) but the cross-animal ITI result depends on extrapolated licks (.07 in range). Within a known animal the calendar already tracks recovery (blocked .75; balance adds little, .76): a STATE MARKER, not a forecast (no prediction of the next session's change, p .24-.80). CAVEAT (10-29): for CUED licks the shift is largely the landing error seen through a target code (S3); ITI keeps a genuine state shift; docked-spout ITI licks do not show the ITI balance (moving-spout result). Window and pool chosen on these data, selection cross-validated; 4 animals. Script scripts/lick_recovery_primary.py. PROVISIONAL.

notes: Hidden supplement. Encoding page Fig 14.17 [#f-lick_balance_explainer] (Priya 10-28: 'build in an explanation of how it's calculated'). Which licks: cued = the FIRST lick after the cue; ITI = every lick after >= 2 s without licking. Response: ALM, tjM1, SSp-m, SSp-n, SSs per hemisphere, mean dF/F 0.1-0.5 s after the lick minus -1.0..-0.5 s. Prediction: a line of each area's response against lick angle from the same animal's PRE licks. GAIN = sum observed / sum predicted per hemisphere; BALANCE = log2(contra gain) - log2(ipsi gain). PS94 acute PS94_0817 contralesional 2.08, ipsilesional 4.26 -> -1.04; chronic PS94_1005 0.98 / 1.13 -> -0.20. Caveat: acute licks land at -20 to -45 deg, mostly outside the pre range, where the line is extrapolated (33 % of acute first licks); in-range only, the cued marker survives (.53) but the ITI cross-animal result does not (.07).

shapes.name: TextBox 5
paragraphs: Sessions binned by day; faint = each animal, line = mean of animals, band = 95 % CI (animals → sessions); A relative to the animal's pre; B aim change vs own pre (+ = contralesional)

notes: Encoding page Fig 0.12 [#f-recovery_timing_pooled_day_lick] (image recovery_timing_pooled_day_lick_aim.png, both panels). A: far-contra hit rate and the far-contra frozen code on hits, each relative to the animal's pre; both climb together to ~0.8 by day ~9, then behavior completes (~1.0) while cortex stays at ~0.7 (the gap opens chronically, not acutely; days 1-5 of the cortex line rest on few animals / sessions). B (10-30): far-contra AIM (first post-cue lick, 3-D angle minus the animal's pre mean at that spout, + = contralesional; all trials with a first lick, so acute aim is mostly failed attempts): -32 deg day 1, -15 days 6-7, -9 days 8-9 (half-recovery 3-5 days), then about -5 to -6 deg from day 25 on, CI below 0 in every late bin. Fraction of the acute aim deficit recovered by chronic: PS92 .84, PS93 .76, PS94 .55, PS95 .90 (hit rate ~1.0 in all); the chronic residual is mostly PS94 (-14 to -18 deg), the animal with the least code recovery too (descriptive, n = 4). Trace = Allen-area mean dF/F % (adopted hemo-corrected SVD) minus a 2-s running median, with the face regressed out (own-session FaceRhythm factors + 20 face-point PCs + speeds, lags +/-0.3 s, out-of-fold ridge). Event = peak whose height above the median of the preceding 1.0-0.2 s exceeds 4 x the animal's August-pre robust SD; up and down. Orofacial = ALM, tjM1, SSp-m, SSp-n; limb = SSp-ul, SSp-ll. Orofacial events / min pre -> acute: PS92 3.7 -> 22.3, PS93 8.1 -> 43.4, PS94 4.4 -> 23.4, PS95 3.7 -> 21.2 (4/4); LMM x6.7 acute, x3.1 subacute, x1.5 chronic (q <= 0.009); raw x5.3. DAQ-contact-only quiet frames gave x5.1 / x2.5 / x1.4, so excluding non-contact licks makes it LARGER. Limb also up, acutely only in PS93 / PS95. Caveat: k = 4 was chosen to separate pre from acute, so the acute contrast is optimistic (subacute / chronic were not used). Pre-stroke the same event type (same map) is rare in engaged quiet (0.1-0.5 /min) and 8-60x more frequent in the quit period. No ipsilesional bias in rate or amplitude (ipsi - contra +0.02 n.s.). Encoding page Fig 13.6 [#f-lick_matched_gauss_perspout] (docked ITI; first-lick rows 2 and 4 on the page). All-ITI caption: contralesional after 5 of 6 spouts acutely (+0.30 to +0.49, 4/4 each; close contra +0.19 n.s.) and after close mid, far ipsi, far mid in every epoch (close mid +0.43 / +0.18 / +0.24; far ipsi +0.49 / +0.42 / +0.42; far mid +0.35 / +0.28 / +0.28); ITI first lick of each bout positive at every spout and epoch (acute +0.25 to +0.54, 4/4). Cued: far contra +0.22 acute (4/4), then -0.09 n.s. / -0.27 [-0.39, -0.14] (4/4, ipsilesional chronically); close ipsi +0.30 acute, +0.14 chronic (3/4); close mid +0.18 and far ipsi +0.14 acute (4/4). SIGN: + = READ more contralesional than the lick landed (decoder like-for-like offset, a DIRECTION quantity; page sign-conventions box); landing / decoded lateral position + = contralesional; image left = ipsilesional. Decoder: frozen pre-stroke KEY-row lateral lick-position decoder per lick set (z-scored Allen areas with the ALM / tjM1 split, lags 0-0.2 s, August pre sessions, pre scored leave-one-session-out). Licks: LP video licks (cam4 detector) with 3-D tongue position from cam1 + cam4 pose. LIKE-FOR-LIKE offset = each lick's decoded lateral position minus a Gaussian-weighted mean (sigma 0.1 mm, chosen by held-out pre prediction) of the decoded positions of the animal's PRE licks of the same set that LANDED at the same lateral place (any spout, no bins); 0.5 % of licks without a reference. Session means; change vs pre, 95 % paired nested bootstrap (animals -> sessions), * = CI excludes 0, k/n animals. ITI = licks between trials; DOCKED-SPOUT ITI = onset while the spout is docked (~35 % of ITI licks; Priya's primary ITI set, 10-29; frozen all-ITI decoder, nothing refit). PROVISIONAL (n = 4).
